title: Direct observation of phonon mode with an antisymmetric Raman tensor
authors: Shangfei Wu, Shang Ren, Kai Du, Xianghan Xu, Sang-Wook Cheong, David Vanderbilt, Girsh Blumberg
abstract: Phonon angular momentum, characterized by circular or elliptical motion of atoms, plays a decisive role in diverse phenomena, ranging from the phonon Hall effect, phonon magnetic moment, Einstein-de Haas effect, Weyl phonons, and driven chiral phonons. The phonon modes with an antisymmetric Raman tensor, which carry an intrinsic phonon angular momentum in a pseudovector symmetry channel, have been overlooked in the past in the chiral phonon community. Here, we report the detection of this type of phonon mode using polarization-resolved Raman spectroscopy. We observe a phonon at 266cm$^{-1}$ in the antiferromagnetic chiral phase of Cr$_2$O$_3$ in the $A_2$-pseudovector symmetry channel. This $A_2$ mode's frequency and the elliptical motion are captured by first-principles phonon calculations, which treat both lattice and spins on an equal footing as 'slow' degrees of freedom. This mode gets Raman activity due to the presence of Cr vacancies in Cr$_2$O$_3$ that locally break the twofold rotational symmetry perpendicular to the threefold axis. Our results provide a new way to detect the novel symmetry-forbidden $A_2$ phonon modes with an antisymmetric Raman tensor in a pseudovector symmetry channel.
summary: This work reports the direct observation of a novel phonon mode in Cr2O3 using polarization-resolved Raman spectroscopy. The mode possesses an antisymmetric Raman tensor and carries intrinsic phonon angular momentum. By combining experiment with first-principles calculations, the authors establish a new technique to study symmetry-protected chiral excitations in quantum magnets.
main_problem: The study aims to detect and characterize phonon modes that possess an intrinsic phonon angular momentum (PAM) and are associated with an antisymmetric Raman tensor, as these modes are typically overlooked in standard spectroscopic analyses.
main_result: The authors successfully detected an A2 phonon mode at 266 cm-1 in the antiferromagnetic chiral phase of Cr2O3, confirming its existence via polarization-resolved Raman spectroscopy.
method: The research combines polarization-resolved Raman spectroscopy with first-principles phonon calculations that treat both lattice vibrations and magnetic spins as coupled 'slow' degrees of freedom.
model_or_system: The physical system is Cr2O3, particularly when it enters its antiferromagnetic (AFM) chiral phase. The analysis relies on group theory to track symmetry breaking from the high-temperature phase (D3d) to the low-temperature magnetic phase (D3).
key_observables: Phonon frequency (266 cm-1), polarization dependence (Raman tensor symmetry), and the presence of non-zero atom-resolved Phonon Angular Momentum (PAM).
important_parameters: Temperature (especially the Néel temperature, T_N), and the presence of local symmetry breaking due to Cr vacancies.
main_assumptions: The Raman activity of the otherwise symmetry-forbidden A2 mode is attributed to local symmetry breaking caused by Cr vacancies in the crystal structure.
figures_summary: Figures show the polarization dependence of the 266 cm-1 mode, and the calculations visualize the temperature dependence and the non-zero atom-resolved PAM for the A2 mode.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the theoretical necessity of detecting antisymmetric Raman tensor modes, presents the experimental detection in Cr2O3, and supports the findings with detailed first-principles calculations linking the mode's activity to structural defects.
why_interesting: The methodology provides a novel spectroscopic handle (antisymmetric Raman tensor) to probe chiral excitations and intrinsic angular momentum in magnetic materials, which is highly relevant to understanding complex quantum magnetic ordering.
